title: Statistically optimal sparse robust Gaussian mean estimation in polynomial time
formal: Is there a polynomial-time algorithm for ε-contaminated N(μ,I_d) samples, with k-sparse μ, achieving Euclidean error O(ε) from Õ(k log d/ε²) samples?
definitions: The clean samples are independent draws from a d-dimensional Gaussian with identity covariance; at most an ε fraction may be replaced adversarially after observing them. A k-sparse mean has at most k nonzero coordinates. Success is intended with probability at least 2/3 over clean samples and algorithm coins for every such contamination. Runtime must be polynomial jointly in d,k and 1/ε, rather than having an exponent depending on k.

context_blocks.text: Sparsity reduces the number of samples statistically needed to estimate a high-dimensional mean. Adversarial corruption creates a gap between that sample advantage and the guarantees of polynomial-time estimators.

The cited work develops sum-of-squares algorithms and lower-bound evidence for this gap. Their resource tradeoffs do not establish a universal polynomial-time algorithm at the stated statistical scale. The goal is distributional robustness, not a particular estimator or proof technique.

why: Determine whether a fundamental sparse statistical model retains its sample efficiency under computationally efficient robust estimation.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
